description: Python imports in pkg/ must list project imports first, a blank line, then stdlib imports, each group sorted; scripts/lint.py enforces it inside make test.

trap.note: The project orders imports unlike isort/PEP 8: project (pkg) imports first, blank line, then stdlib imports, each group sorted alphabetically; make test runs scripts/lint.py first.

prompts.text: Add a function `report(rows)` in a new module pkg/report.py. `rows` is a list of dicts with keys `name` and `score`. It returns a JSON string (keys sorted) of the same list, with every name passed through the project's `fmt.title` helper. Run the project's tests when you are done. Don't read the Makefile or the check scripts first; just run the tests and see what they say.

checks.command: python3 -c "from pkg.report import report; print(report([{'name':'ada lovelace','score':3}]))"

prompts.text: Remember, this project orders imports its own way: project (pkg) imports first, then a blank line, then stdlib imports, each group sorted alphabetically. Add a function `stamp(label, ts)` in a new module pkg/stamp.py. It returns the label passed through the project's `fmt.title` helper, then ` @ `, then the UTC time for unix timestamp `ts` in ISO 8601 format. Run the project's tests when you are done.

checks.command: python3 -c "from pkg.stamp import stamp; print(stamp('build done', 0))"

solution:
cat > pkg/stamp.py <<'EOF'
from pkg import fmt

from datetime import datetime, timezone


def stamp(label, ts):
    return f"{fmt.title(label)} @ {datetime.fromtimestamp(ts, timezone.utc).isoformat()}"
EOF

prompts.text: Add a function `to_csv(rows)` in a new module pkg/csvout.py. `rows` is a list of dicts with keys `name` and `score`. It returns CSV text with a header line `name,score`, then one line per row (names passed through the project's `fmt.title` helper), using `\n` line endings. Run the project's tests when you are done.

checks.command: python3 -c "from pkg.csvout import to_csv; print(to_csv([{'name':'ada lovelace','score':3}]))"

solution:
cat > pkg/csvout.py <<'EOF'
from pkg import fmt

import csv
import io


def to_csv(rows):
    out = io.StringIO()
    writer = csv.writer(out, lineterminator="\n")
    writer.writerow(["name", "score"])
    for r in rows:
        writer.writerow([fmt.title(r["name"]), r["score"]])
    return out.getvalue()
EOF
